info.name: Mess_Tally
info.description:
Postman collection for the MessTally backend. It mirrors every route currently mounted in `src/app.ts`: `/api/v1/auth`, `/api/v1/profile`, `/api/v1/mess` (including the `/mess/members` and `/mess/leave` routes), `/api/v1/months`, `/api/v1/meals`, the bazar, utilities and utility fund deposit routes, and the root health route. Planned modules that are not mounted yet (summary, dashboard, AI) are intentionally absent.

Base URL comes from the `baseUrl` collection variable (default `http://localhost:8000`, matching `PORT` in `.env`).

Auth flow: Register sends an OTP, Verify Email creates the user and returns tokens, and Login/Refresh Token return a fresh token pair. Login, Verify Email, and Refresh Token set the `accessToken` and `refreshToken` httpOnly cookies; the Login and Refresh Token test scripts also copy the tokens plus `activeMessId`/`mess` into collection variables.

Mess scope: tokens carry identity only (`userId`, `name`, `email`, `role`). There is no `messId` claim and no mess-switch endpoint. The server reads `user.activeMessId`, verifies the matching `mess_member` row is `ACTIVE`, and only then runs the mess-scoped action. Create Mess, Join Mess, and Approve Member maintain that pointer; Leave Mess and Remove Member clear it.

Protected requests accept the access token from the cookie jar or from the `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}` header. Create Mess, Join Mess, and My Messes require `Role.USER`; the other protected routes accept any authenticated role, but mess-scoped actions still need a valid ACTIVE membership. `Refresh Token` reads the `refreshToken` httpOnly cookie, so run Login or Verify Email earlier in the same Postman session.

request.description:
Validates the email with Zod, including a DNS MX lookup (domains that cannot receive mail, such as `gmail.co` or `example.com`, are rejected), stores the pending registration in Redis and emails a 6-digit OTP (valid for 5 minutes). The pending registration itself is kept for 1 hour so a new code can be requested after the OTP expires. The user is only created after Verify Email.

The sample body uses a real Gmail address because `example.com` publishes a null MX record and would be rejected.

A 60-second cooldown is enforced per email, so an immediate second Register call returns `429`.

Responds `201` with `data: { email, purpose, expiresInSeconds, resendAvailableInSeconds, resendsRemaining }` (`300`, `60` and `3`). No tokens are issued yet.

In development the OTP is also printed in the server console as `[dev] OTP <email> : <otp>`.

Validates the registration OTP, creates the user, sends the welcome email, and sets `accessToken` and `refreshToken` httpOnly cookies. Responds `201` with `data: { user, accessToken, refreshToken }`; the new user starts with `activeMessId: null`.

If the code has expired the API returns `Verification code has expired. Please request a new one.` — call Resend OTP with `purpose: "REGISTRATION"` to get a fresh code, since the pending registration survives for 1 hour. After 5 wrong codes the OTP is invalidated and the response is `429`.

Other errors: `400` when there is no pending registration, `409` when the email is already verified, and `403` for suspended or deleted users.

The test script stores both tokens in collection variables.

Re-issues a 6-digit OTP when the previous one expired. `purpose` must be `REGISTRATION` (after Register) or `FORGOT_PASSWORD` (after Forgot Password).

The route only works when that flow is already pending. Without the Redis session created by Register or Forgot Password it returns `400` and sends nothing, so it cannot be called randomly.

Limits per email + purpose:
- `429` while the 60-second cooldown is still running; the message includes the seconds left.
- `429` after 3 resends in the same session; restart the flow with Register or Forgot Password.

The previous code is invalidated immediately. Responds `200` with `data: { email, purpose, expiresInSeconds, resendAvailableInSeconds, resendsRemaining }`, where `resendsRemaining` is counted after this resend.

Other errors: `409` if the registration email has since been registered, and for `FORGOT_PASSWORD` `403` when the account is suspended, deleted or unverified, plus `404` when the user no longer exists.

Logs in with email and password. Unknown emails return `404`, suspended or deleted accounts `403`, and a wrong password `401`. Email verification is not re-checked at login.

On success it sets `accessToken` and `refreshToken` httpOnly cookies and responds `200` with `data: { accessToken, refreshToken, activeMessId, mess }`. `mess` is the summary of the active mess (`id`, `name`, `roomCode`, `currency`, `isJoinable`, `requireApproval`, `mealCutoffTime`) or `null`.

The test script stores both tokens and syncs `activeMessId`, `messId`, `roomCode`, and `messName` from the response.

Returns the authenticated user's full account: `id`, `email`, `emailVerified`, `name`, `role`, `status`, `isDeleted`, `deletedAt`, `activeMessId`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, and the nested `profile` (`bio`, `phone`, `address`, `imageUrl`, `imagePublicId`). The password is omitted. Responds `200`.

Requires a valid access token, supplied either by the `accessToken` cookie set during Login / Verify Email or by the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. The route is protected by `auth(Role.USER, Role.ADMIN, Role.SUPERADMIN)`.

Issues a new access token and refresh token using the `refreshToken` httpOnly cookie. No request body is required and the controller does not read an Authorization header — run Login or Verify Email first so Postman has the refresh cookie (Create Mess no longer issues tokens).

Responds `200` with `data: { accessToken, refreshToken, activeMessId, mess }`; `mess` is the active mess summary or `null`. The refresh token is rotated and both cookies are reset. The test script updates both tokens and syncs `activeMessId`, `messId`, `roomCode`, and `messName`.

Sends a 6-digit password reset OTP to the email (valid for 5 minutes). The OTP is stored in Redis under `user-forgetPassword-otp:<email>`, and a 1-hour `user-forgetPassword-session:<email>` marker records that a reset is pending so the code can be re-sent later.

Only existing, email-verified, non-deleted accounts that are not suspended can request a reset. Unknown email `404`; suspended, deleted or unverified `403`. A 60-second cooldown is enforced, so an immediate repeat call returns `429`. In development the OTP is printed in the server console.

Responds `200` with `data: { email, purpose, expiresInSeconds, resendAvailableInSeconds, resendsRemaining }`.

If the code expires, call Resend OTP with `purpose: "FORGOT_PASSWORD"`, then use the received OTP with Reset Password.

Verifies the password reset OTP sent by Forgot Password and updates the user's password.

The OTP must match `user-forgetPassword-otp:<email>` in Redis and expires after 5 minutes; once expired the API returns `Password reset code has expired. Please request a new one.` After 5 wrong codes the OTP is invalidated and the response is `429`.

Errors: `404` unknown email, `403` for suspended, deleted or unverified users.

A successful reset clears the pending session marker and the resend limits, so a later Forgot Password request starts with 3 fresh resends. A password-reset confirmation email is sent to the user after the password is updated. Responds `200` with `data: null`.

Updates the authenticated user's profile row. Provide at least one of `bio`, `phone`, or `address`.

- `bio`: up to 500 characters; `""` clears it.
- `phone`: up to 20 characters and must match `+?[0-9\s()-]{6,20}`, so it cannot be cleared with an empty string.
- `address`: up to 255 characters; `""` clears it.

Fields are trimmed before saving. Responds `200` with the updated profile row (`bio`, `phone`, `address`, `imageUrl`, `imagePublicId`, timestamps).

Requires a valid access token and an active, email-verified account. The route is protected by `auth(Role.USER, Role.ADMIN, Role.SUPERADMIN)`.

Uploads or replaces the authenticated user's profile image. Responds `201` with the updated profile row.

Send the image as `multipart/form-data` using the `profileImage` field. Only JPEG, PNG, and WebP images are accepted, with a maximum size of 5 MB; other types return `400` and oversize files `413`. The previous Cloudinary image is deleted after a successful replacement.

**Before sending, select an actual image file in the `profileImage` field.** The previously saved sample path no longer exists in the repository; if the field is left empty, Postman fails locally with `EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, read` and the request never reaches the server. The request method must be `PATCH`.

Requires a valid access token and an active, non-deleted account. The route is protected by `auth(Role.USER, Role.ADMIN, Role.SUPERADMIN)`.

body.raw:
{
  "name": "Sunrise Mess",
  "address": "House 12, Road 3, Dhanmondi, Dhaka",
  "currency": "BDT",
  "mealCutoffTime": "11:00",
  "isJoinable": true,
  "requireApproval": true
}

request.description:
Creates a mess and makes the logged-in user its OWNER (also flagged as manager and ACTIVE). Protected by `auth(Role.USER)`, so ADMIN and SUPERADMIN accounts receive `403`.

Only `name` is required; `address`, `currency`, `mealCutoffTime`, `isJoinable`, and `requireApproval` are optional. Server defaults: `currency` = "BDT", `mealCutoffTime` = "11:00", `isJoinable` = true, `requireApproval` = true. `name` is trimmed, `currency` is uppercased, and an empty `address` is stored as `null`.

A user can only be ACTIVE in one mess: if the caller already has an ACTIVE membership, this returns `409 Conflict` and asks them to leave that mess first. A blank name returns `400`, an inactive user `403`, and a missing user `404`.

The server pulls the next integer from the `mess_room_code_seq` PostgreSQL sequence and encodes it with Sqids, prefixed by the first three letters of the mess name after stripping non-letters (padded with `X`), e.g. "Sunrise Mess" -> `SUN-JEVTDKRA`. In one transaction it creates the mess, the OWNER membership, and sets `user.activeMessId`.

Responds `201` with `data: { mess, activeMessId }`. `mess` includes its `members` array (the new OWNER row) plus `plan`, `planExpiresAt`, and timestamps. **No tokens or cookies are issued here**: tokens are identity-only and come from Login/Verify Email/Refresh Token. The test script stores `messId`, `activeMessId`, `roomCode`, and `messName`.

Joins an existing mess using its `roomCode` (trimmed and uppercased). Protected by `auth(Role.USER)`, so ADMIN and SUPERADMIN accounts receive `403`; `validateRequest` requires a non-empty code of at most 64 characters.

Responds `201` with `data: { mess, membership, activeMessId }`. The membership is `PENDING` when the mess has `requireApproval = true` (then `activeMessId` is `null`), otherwise `ACTIVE` and `user.activeMessId` is set to this mess.

No tokens are issued here. Errors: `404` unknown room code, `403` when `isJoinable = false`, and `409` when the user already has an ACTIVE membership (here or in another mess) or a PENDING request for this mess. A previous `LEFT` or `REJECTED` row is reused and reset to `MEMBER`, `isManager: false`, `rentShare: 1.0`, `fixedRentAmount: null`, `joinedAt: now`, `leftAt: null`.

Run Create Mess first to populate `roomCode`, but use an account that is not ACTIVE in another mess. The test script stores `joinedMessId`, `membershipId`, `membershipStatus`, and `activeMessId`.

Lists every mess the logged-in user belongs to, for the mess picker. Protected by `auth(Role.USER)`; this endpoint must stay usable when the caller has no active mess, so it never calls `requireActiveMembership`.

Responds `200` with `{ activeMessId, messes[] }`. Each row carries `membershipId`, `role`, `status`, `isManager`, `joinedAt`, `leftAt`, `isActive`, and a `mess` summary (`id`, `name`, `address`, `currency`, `roomCode`, `isJoinable`, `requireApproval`, `mealCutoffTime`).

Rows are `ACTIVE` first, then `PENDING`, then `LEFT` (newest first within each group); `REJECTED` is excluded. `isActive` marks the one mess pointed at by `user.activeMessId`, and `activeMessId` is `null` when that pointer is missing or stale (no matching `ACTIVE` membership), so the token/JWT is never trusted for scope.

The test script asserts the list shape and syncs `activeMessId` (or unsets it when null).

query.description: Optional. Enable to return only rows with this status (PENDING | ACTIVE | LEFT | REJECTED). Leave disabled for the full member list.

request.description:
Lists every `mess_member` row of the caller's active mess (all statuses by default), sorted `ACTIVE` -> `PENDING` -> `LEFT` -> `REJECTED` and oldest first within each group. Any authenticated user with an ACTIVE membership may call it; callers without one get `403`.

The optional `?status=ACTIVE` filter is what the meals, bazar and utility dropdowns use (AC 2.1.2). An invalid status value returns `400`.

Responds `200` with `{ members[], total }`. Each row has `id` (the `mess_member` id used by every other endpoint), `userId`, `name`, `email`, `avatarUrl`, `role`, `status`, `isManager`, `rentShare`, `fixedRentAmount` (number or `null`), `joinedAt`, and `leftAt`.

The test script stores the first ACTIVE non-owner member as `memberId`, which is the target used by Transfer Manager, Transfer Ownership and Remove Member.

Manager only (`is_manager = true`). Lists `PENDING` join requests for the caller's active mess, oldest first.

Responds `200` with `{ members[], total }` in the same shape as List Members. A non-manager gets `403`, and so does a caller without a valid ACTIVE membership.

The test script stores the first request as `pendingMemberId`.

Manager only. Moves a `PENDING` join request to `ACTIVE`, sets `isManager: false`, stamps `joinedAt`, clears `leftAt`, and points `user.activeMessId` at this mess (PRD 2.1).

Scoped by mess: a member id from another mess returns `404`; a row that is not `PENDING` returns `409`. Because a user can be ACTIVE in only one mess (D14), approval is also rejected with `409` when the user has become active in another mess in the meantime.

Responds `200` with the updated member row (same shape as List Members).

Manager only. Moves a `PENDING` join request to `REJECTED` and clears `isManager`. The row is kept (D10) so a later join reuses it; rejected rows are excluded from all calculations and dropdowns. If the rejected user's `activeMessId` points at this mess, it is cleared defensively.

`404` when the id is not in the caller's mess, `409` when the row is not `PENDING`. Responds `200` with the updated member row.

Transfers the manager position to the target ACTIVE member. The caller gives up `is_manager` and the target receives it, so a mess never has more than one manager. A manager can hand the position to another member; if the caller is the OWNER, `role` stays `OWNER` and only the manager flag moves. The OWNER can also call this when they no longer hold the flag, so a mess can never be stuck without a manager (for example after a manager leaves). Ownership itself is a separate action: `PATCH /api/v1/mess/members/:id/owner`.

No request body is needed. The target must be an ACTIVE member of the caller's mess and cannot be the caller (`400`). Plain members get `403`, unknown or cross-mess ids `404`, non-active targets `409`. Responds `200` with the target row (`isManager: true`); refetch `GET /api/v1/mess/members` to see the previous manager's row as `false`.

exec: pm.test("exactly one OWNER and one manager remain", () => {

request.description:
OWNER only. Moves the OWNER role to an ACTIVE member of the same mess: the target becomes `OWNER` with `isManager: true`, and the previous owner becomes a `MEMBER` with `isManager: false`, so exactly one owner and one manager remain. The current owner is demoted before the target is promoted so the `mess_member_one_owner_idx` partial unique index is never violated.

Run this before `POST /api/v1/mess/leave` when the mess still has other active members; leaving as the owner returns `409` until ownership is transferred. The target must be ACTIVE, in the same mess, and not the caller (`400`). A non-owner caller gets `403`, unknown or cross-mess ids `404`, non-active targets `409`. Responds `200` with the new owner's member row.

Leaves the caller's active mess: sets `status = LEFT`, stamps `leftAt`, clears `isManager`, and nulls `user.activeMessId`. Switching messes means leaving and then joining another (D7); there is no switch endpoint.

An OWNER with other ACTIVE members must first transfer ownership with `PATCH /api/v1/mess/members/:id/owner` (`409` otherwise); the last active member can always leave. Callers without a valid ACTIVE membership get `403`. Responds `200` with `{ messId, leftAt, activeMessId: null }`.

Manager only hard delete, reserved for members with no records at all (AC 2.1.3). Blocked with `409` when meal entries, bazar, deposits, utility bills or payments reference the member; the message lists the counts and suggests setting `status = LEFT` instead (D12).

The owner cannot be removed (`403`) and a manager cannot remove themselves (`400`, use Leave). A member id from another mess returns `404`. Responds `200` with `{ id, deleted: true }`.

Lists every month of the caller's active mess, newest first. Mess scope comes from `user.activeMessId`; no mess id is sent by the client and none is added to the JWT. Each row returns `id`, `name` (`YYYY-MM`), `startDate`, `endDate`, `status` (`ACTIVE` / `CLOSED`), `managerId`, `closedAt` and `isCurrent`. Requires an ACTIVE membership (`403` otherwise).

Manager only. Opens a calendar month explicitly (D1). Responds `201` with `{ month, created: true }` on the first open and `200` with `created: false` if the month is already ACTIVE. A CLOSED month returns `409` because reopening is a Phase 4 action. Non-managers get `403`. Meals also auto-create the month on first write, so this endpoint is for explicit control.

Returns the dense meal grid for a month: every day, every ACTIVE member (plus LEFT members who have data, flagged read-only), per-member totals and `houseTotals` (AC 3.1.1). `?month=YYYY-MM` is optional and defaults to the current UTC month. A month with no row is still a `200`: `month.exists = false`, `month.id = null`, all cells zero. This read never creates a `mess_month` row. Requires an ACTIVE membership.

Upserts one grid cell (AC 3.1.2, AC 3.1.5). `PUT` replaces the whole cell, so all four counts are required; values must be finite and `>= 0` (AC 3.1.3). The month is derived from `date` and auto-created on first write. A date in a previous month is accepted and lands in that month. Cross-mess member ids return `404`; non-active members return `409`; a CLOSED month or a locked entry returns `409`. Idempotent: repeating the same payload leaves one row. Responds `200` with `{ entry }`.

Daily-sheet bulk entry: one shared `date` plus 1-200 members, written in one transaction. Duplicate member ids are rejected with `400`. Any missing/cross-mess member (`404`), non-active member (`409`), CLOSED month (`409`) or locked existing cell (`409`) rolls back the whole batch. Responds `200` with `{ entries }`.

Deletes one meal entry. The row is looked up by id AND the caller's mess, so a cross-mess id returns `404`. A CLOSED month or a locked entry returns `409`. Responds `200` with `{ id, deleted: true }`.

Lists bazar entries for one month with `houseTotal` and per-shopper totals (AC 4.1.2). `?month=YYYY-MM` is optional and defaults to the current UTC month. `from`/`to` are optional inclusive date filters inside the month; `shopperId` filters to one member. Ordering is `bazarDate` then `createdAt`, ascending. A month with no row still returns `200` with `month.exists = false` and zero totals — GET never creates a month. Any ACTIVE member can read. The test script stores the selected month and the first entry id.

Any ACTIVE member can record a bazar trip. `title` is optional and defaults to `"Bazar"`; `items` is optional free text. `amount` must be finite, `> 0`, at most 2 decimals and max `99,999,999.99`. `shopperId` must be an ACTIVE member of the caller's mess (`404` cross-mess, `409` non-active). The month is derived from `bazarDate` and auto-created on first write; a CLOSED month returns `409`. `addedById` is the caller and `paidFromMessFund` is forced `false` — neither is accepted from the body. Run Get Meal Grid first so `{{memberId}}` is populated, and set `{{entryDate}}` to a date in the selected month. Responds `201` with `{ entry }`.

Partial update; at least one of `title`, `items`, `amount`, `bazarDate`, `shopperId` is required. `items: null` clears the text. Changing `bazarDate` across a month boundary moves the entry to the target month — both the old and target months must be ACTIVE (`409` otherwise). A cross-mess id returns `404`. `addedById` and `paidFromMessFund` cannot be changed. Responds `200` with `{ entry }`.
Deletes one bazar entry. The row is looked up by id AND the caller's mess, so a cross-mess id returns `404`. A CLOSED month returns `409`. Responds `200` with `{ id, deleted: true }`.

Lists utility bills for one month plus totals (AC 5.1.2, AC 5.1.3). `?month=YYYY-MM` is optional and defaults to the current UTC month. `totals` contains `total`, `paid`, `unpaid`, `activeMemberCount` and `perPersonShare` (formula U1: total ÷ ACTIVE members, rounded to 2 decimals, `0` when there are no active members). A month with no row still returns `200` with `month.exists = false` and zero totals. GET never creates a month. Utility data never affects meals, bazar or settlement. The test script stores the selected month and the first bill id.

Any ACTIVE member can add a bill. `month` is required because bills have no natural date; the month is auto-created on first write and a CLOSED month returns `409`. `category` defaults to `OTHER`; `splitType` defaults to `EQUAL` and `CUSTOM_WEIGHT` is rejected with `400`. `dueDate` and `notes` may be `null`. New bills are always unpaid; payment state changes only through `PATCH /:id/paid`. `paymentId`, `receiptUrl`, `paidAt` and `paidById` are never accepted, and `addedById` is the caller. Responds `201` with `{ bill }`.

Partial update of one bill; at least one of `category`, `title`, `amount`, `splitType`, `dueDate`, `notes` is required. `dueDate` and `notes` accept `null` to clear. A bill cannot move between months here — delete and recreate if the month is wrong. Payment fields are not editable. A cross-mess id returns `404` and a CLOSED month returns `409`. Responds `200` with `{ bill }`.

Marks a bill paid: `isPaid = true`, `paidAt = now`, `paidById = caller`. Kept as one endpoint so `isPaid` and `paidAt` always agree with the DB CHECK constraint. A CLOSED month returns `409`. Responds `200` with `{ bill }`.
Marks a bill unpaid and clears `paidAt` and `paidById` together, so the DB CHECK constraint stays satisfied. A CLOSED month returns `409`. Responds `200` with `{ bill }`.
Deletes one utility bill. Scoped by id AND the caller's mess (`404` cross-mess). A CLOSED month returns `409`. Responds `200` with `{ id, deleted: true }`.

Lists utility fund deposits for one month with the total and per-member totals. Any ACTIVE member can read this for transparency. `?month=YYYY-MM` is optional and defaults to the current UTC month; a month with no row still returns `200` with `month.exists = false`, an empty list and `total: 0`. GET never creates a month. Multiple deposits per member and month are allowed. The test script stores the selected month and the first deposit id.

Manager only (`403` for a non-manager). Records a utility fund deposit for an ACTIVE member of the caller's mess (`404` cross-mess, `409` non-active). `date` is optional and defaults to today in UTC; the month is derived from it and auto-created on first write. A CLOSED month returns `409`. `receivedById` is the caller and is never accepted from the body. Multiple deposits per member per month are allowed. Run Get Meal Grid first so `{{memberId}}` is populated. Responds `201` with `{ deposit }`.

Manager only. Partial update of one deposit; at least one of `memberId`, `amount`, `date`, `note` is required. `note: null` clears the note. Changing `date` across a month boundary moves the deposit to the target month — both months must be ACTIVE (`409` otherwise). `receivedById` never changes. A cross-mess id returns `404`. Responds `200` with `{ deposit }`.
Manager only. Deletes one deposit, scoped by id AND the caller's mess (`404` cross-mess). A CLOSED month returns `409`. Responds `200` with `{ id, deleted: true }`.
Basic health/welcome route. Responds `200` with `{ success: true, message: "Welcome to MessTally" }`; it is registered directly on the app, so there is no `statusCode`/`data` wrapper.
